The '''2022 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022 to elect members of [[Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council]]. This was on the same day as [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections]]. 17 of the 51 seats were up for election.<ref>{{cite web |title=Election timetable in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england#metropolitan-districts |website=GOV.UK |access-date=7 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Background==
Since its creation in 1974, Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council has always had the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] as the largest party. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] came the closest to overtaking them in [[1996 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election|1996]], when they won 16 seats to the Conservatives' 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=http://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Solihull-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=8 April 2022 |page=12}}</ref> In the [[2021 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election|2021 election]], the Conservatives gained three seats on a vote share of 53.8% (+7.9), the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] gained 1 seat with 20.5% of the vote (-5.1), the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] lost 3 seats on 12.2% (-1.3), and Labour lost 1 seat on 12.9% (+0.9).

The seats up for election in 2022 were last elected in [[2018 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election|2018]]. In that election, the Conservatives won 49.1% of votes and gained 2 seats from the Liberal Democrats, the Greens gained 1 seat from the Conservatives and won 25.1% of the votes, Labour gained 1 seat from [[UK Independence Party|UKIP]] and won 15.5%, and the Liberal Democrats lost 1 seat and achieved 11.9%.<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project - 2018 - Solihull |url=http://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/results/2018/61/ |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=8 April 2022}}</ref>

Changes:
* September 2021: Angela Sandison suspended from the Conservatives<ref>{{cite news |title=Solihull councillor suspended by Tory party over autism comments |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-58728360 |access-date=8 April 2022 |work=BBC News |date=29 September 2021}}</ref>
* October 2021: David Cole joins Conservatives from Labour, and Marcus Brain joins Greens from Labour<ref>{{cite news |last1=Madeley |first1=Peter |title=Labour wiped out on West Midlands authority as councillors cross floor |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/news/politics/2021/10/29/labour-wiped-out-on-west-midlands-authority-as-councillors-cross-floor/ |access-date=8 April 2022 |work=Express and Star |language=en |date=29 October 2022}}</ref>
* November 2021: Cheryl Buxton-Sait (Green) resigns from council; seat left vacant until 2022 election<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collis |first1=Emily |title=Green councillor resigns to help under pressure NHS |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/green-councillor-resigns-solihull-council-22263676 |access-date=8 April 2022 |work=BirminghamLive |date=29 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref>
* February 2022: Andy Hodgson, Tim Hodgson, and Rosemary Sexton leave Greens<ref>{{cite news |title=Solihull Greens dealt further blows in political row |url=https://solihullobserver.co.uk/news/solihull-greens-dealt-further-blows-in-political-row/ |access-date=8 April 2022 |work=Solihull Observer |date=28 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
